gaps.sentence: She kept every receipt ___ she could claim the expenses back.
gaps.explanation: 'So that + could' expresses purpose; 'in case' expresses precaution.

gaps.sentence: The drug is remarkably effective. ___, it has almost no side effects.
gaps.explanation: 'Furthermore' introduces an additional point supporting the same claim.

gaps.sentence: I enjoyed the film; the ending was weak, ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Though' can come at the end of a sentence as a casual contrast marker; the others cannot.

gaps.sentence: ___ a slight delay in Rome, the whole journey went smoothly.
gaps.explanation: 'Apart from' sets the delay aside as the only problem.

gaps.sentence: Sales fell sharply last quarter; ___, the board cut the dividend.
gaps.explanation: The fall in sales caused the cut: as a result marks the consequence.

gaps.sentence: ___ the fact that the road was icy, the bus kept its usual speed.
gaps.explanation: 'Despite the fact that + clause' concedes a full clause after a preposition.

gaps.sentence: Take a map ___ you get lost in the backstreets.
gaps.explanation: 'In case' = as a precaution against something that might happen.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ the tickets cost more, but they sold out in minutes.
gaps.explanation: After fronted 'Not only', auxiliary inversion applies: Not only did the tickets cost more.
